outcome: composite severe maternal morbidity (SMM) (ICU admission, unplanned hysterectomy, reoperation, eclampsia, blood transfusion)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 223,837 patients with singleton live births in Central New York between 2010 and 2022.
finding: Increasing pre-pregnancy BMI was significantly associated with an increased risk of severe maternal morbidity (SMM) and maternal intensive care unit (ICU) admission.
